name: Phoenix–Tucson Passenger Rail Corridor
funding_status: FRA Corridor Identification and Development (Corridor ID) Program recipient ($500,000 Step 1 Service Development Plan award)
federal_match_program: FRA Federal-State Partnership for Intercity Passenger Rail (80% federal / 20% state-local)

proposed_stations.name: Phoenix Downtown Station
proposed_stations.statutory_housing_regime: AZ HB 2720 / HB 2721 (Casitas by-right & missing middle within 1 mi)
proposed_stations.recommended_redevelopment_focus: High-density mixed-use TOD with ground-floor retail and by-right middle housing

proposed_stations.name: Tempe / ASU Transit Center
proposed_stations.recommended_redevelopment_focus: Student and workforce micro-apartments, car-free living connected to Valley Metro LRT

proposed_stations.name: Chandler Downtown Station
proposed_stations.recommended_redevelopment_focus: Townhouses, residential lot splits, and connected bicycle lanes along canals

proposed_stations.name: Coolidge / Central Pinal County Station
proposed_stations.recommended_redevelopment_focus: Master-planned residential community, industrial logistics park, and primary system railyard

proposed_stations.name: Marana / North Pima Station
proposed_stations.recommended_redevelopment_focus: Park-and-ride commuter housing and active transportation trails along Santa Cruz River

proposed_stations.name: Tucson Historic Depot Station
proposed_stations.statutory_housing_regime: AZ HB 2720 / HB 2721 (Casitas by-right & missing middle within 1 mi)
proposed_stations.recommended_redevelopment_focus: Urban infill housing, historic building adaptive reuse, and Sun Link Streetcar connection

candidate_railyard_sites.name: Coolidge Rail Maintenance & Storage Yard
candidate_railyard_sites.advantages: Flat desert topography, zero urban structure demolition, cost per acre 95% lower than Phoenix/Tucson urban core, direct dual-track junction.
candidate_railyard_sites.siting_recommendation: RECOMMENDED (Primary maintenance & overnight train layover facility)

candidate_railyard_sites.name: Tempe Urban Siding Yard
candidate_railyard_sites.siting_recommendation: NOT RECOMMENDED (Land acquisition costs exceed $170M; site is better utilized for dense mixed-use housing)

name: Austin–San Antonio Passenger Rail (Lone Star Corridor)
funding_status: FRA Corridor ID Step 1 Award ($500k) & Texas Legislature HB 1 study
federal_match_program: FRA Intercity Passenger Rail Partnership + Texas Chapter 311 TIRZ value capture

proposed_stations.name: Austin Downtown / Plaza Saltillo Connection
proposed_stations.statutory_housing_regime: Austin HOME Initiative (3 units by-right, 1,500 sqft lot size minimum, 0 parking)
proposed_stations.recommended_redevelopment_focus: Transit-oriented residential towers, micro-apartments, CapMetro Rail transfer hub

proposed_stations.name: South Austin / Slaughter Station
proposed_stations.recommended_redevelopment_focus: Commercial strip conversion into mixed-income garden apartments and townhomes

proposed_stations.name: San Marcos Station (Texas State University)
proposed_stations.statutory_housing_regime: Texas SB 840 (commercial to residential) & Chapter 214 ADU framework
proposed_stations.recommended_redevelopment_focus: Student and workforce housing with pedestrian connection to campus and Blanco River parks

proposed_stations.name: New Braunfels Station
proposed_stations.recommended_redevelopment_focus: Main street walkable infill, heritage tourism, and commuter housing

proposed_stations.name: San Antonio Sunset Station / Alamodome
proposed_stations.statutory_housing_regime: Texas SB 840 & City of San Antonio Infill Development Zone (IDZ)
proposed_stations.recommended_redevelopment_focus: Historic rail terminal revitalization, affordable housing tax credit partnerships, VIA transit center

candidate_railyard_sites.name: Kyle / San Marcos North Rail Yard
candidate_railyard_sites.advantages: Midpoint corridor location allows balanced fleet deployment to both Austin and San Antonio; low land cost per acre.

candidate_railyard_sites.name: East Austin Urban Yard (Montopolis/Bergstrom)
candidate_railyard_sites.siting_recommendation: NOT RECOMMENDED (Exorbitant land cost of $165M and high community disruption; exurban siding at Kyle saves over $160M)

name: Front Range Passenger Rail (Pueblo–Denver–Fort Collins)
funding_status: FRA Corridor ID Step 1 & Colorado SB 24-184 state transit enterprise funding

proposed_stations.name: Colorado Springs Downtown Station
proposed_stations.recommended_redevelopment_focus: Downtown infill housing, active rail trail connections to Pikes Peak Greenway

candidate_railyard_sites.name: Pueblo Transportation Technology Center Rail Yard
candidate_railyard_sites.advantages: Existing federally certified testing and maintenance trackage; exceptionally low land cost.
